messages:
anya: Heads up — noticed a ~12% p95 latency regression on large-chat traffic after yesterday's kernel-pivots PR.

mike: saw that. Which workloads? can you paste numbers?

anya: p50 42ms -> 44ms, p95 152ms -> 170ms, tokens/sec down 8% for MQA_32 on A100 80G.

raj: I profiled the staging run, flamegraph shows heavier time in memcpy + attention kernel dispatch. attaching short snapshot:
```
hotspots: attention_kernel_generic (54%)
memcpy_kv_shard (18%)
kernel_selector_logic (9%)
```

sara: suspect autotuner picked GQA-optimized kernel for many seq lengths > 512 because of faulty seqlen histogram sampling.

mike: confirmed — runtime sampled by stratified sampler w/ bias towards long seqs. for mixed workloads, GQA path is slower at seq<=256.

anya: are we seeing KV-cache layout impact? some models use paged-kv with 64-block but selector assumes contiguous stride.

raj: yes — when KV layout=interleaved-paged we hit extra remap copies. block_size=64 shows 15% worse memcpy than 128 on our hardware.

sara: proposed quick mitigation: change selector rule => if (layout == paged && avg_seq < 300) prefer short-seq optimized kernel; also add memcpy-aware cost in scoring.

mike: +1. Also add a post-deploy autotune stage that runs short microbenchmarks on node startup to calibrate block_size thresholds.

ci-bot: benchmark run @1898765721
Results:
- model: chat-xl
- hw: a100-80g
- test: mixed-seq (40% <128, 40% 128-512, 20% >512)
- v1 (old selector): p95 150ms, tokens/s 12.5k
- v2 (new rule): p95 158ms, tokens/s 11.9k

anya: that's still regressing overall. are we sure the new rule is applied? maybe the scoring weight for memcpy is too low.

sara: yep. current cost = alpha*kernel_latency + beta*enqueue_overhead. I'll add gamma*memcpy_cost and run local sweep. patch posted: <https://internal.redwood.dev/r/1234>

mike: also let's try block_size=128 for paged-kv by default and see if that helps.

raj: ran quick test: paged block=128 + memcpy-cost tweak -> p95 146ms, tokens/s 12.8k. looks promising.

anya: can we A/B on prod for high-volume customer? low-risk route: route 10% traffic to selector-v2 with memcost tweak + block128.

mike: I'll open rollout PR and add canary metrics (latency by seq bucket, kernel-choice counts, memcpy bytes). cc @sara @raj

sara: ack. adding logs and an extra counter for 'memcopy_bytes' in kernel selector metrics.

ci-bot: scheduled canary deploy at 2026-03-17T17:20Z :rocket:

anya: thanks — if canary looks good we can merge revert-less. otherwise revert the selector change.

mike: timeline — will monitor for 2 hours then report.

raj: adding notes to perf doc: /docs/eng-runtime/kernel-autotune-notes.md :memo:

anya: awesome. keep updates here. :thumbsup:
